title: Leipziger Platz Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **What it is:** the eight-sided square right next to Potsdamer Platz, laid out **1731 to 1734** and named Leipziger Platz in **1814**.
**Why it looks new:** almost every building went up after 1990, but the city rebuilt them on the **old octagon outline**.
**Before the war:** palaces, ministries and **Wertheim**, one of Europe's largest department stores, on the north-east side.
**1961 to 1989:** the square lay in the death strip, and the **inner Wall ran diagonally across it**. A few slabs still stand.
**Today:** the Mall of Berlin stands on the Wertheim site; the old Prussian upper house on Leipziger Straße is now the **Bundesrat**.
**Getting there:** S+U **Potsdamer Platz**, about 100 m away. The Mall is closed on most Sundays, the square never.
**My move:** stop on the middle green, count the eight corners, then find the two pieces of Wall and picture the line between them.
